quote: Theorem 4.1 Let X_{lambda_1}, X_lambda be independent nonnegative random variables with X_{lambda_1} ~ F(lambda_1 t) and X_lambda ~ F(lambda t), where lambda_1, lambda > 0 and F is an absolutely continuous distribution. Let Y_{lambda*_1}, Y_lambda be independent nonnegative random variables with Y_{lambda*_1} ~ F(lambda*_1 t) and Y_lambda ~ F(lambda t), where lambda*_1, lambda > 0. Let r be the reverse hazard rate function of F. Assume tr(t) and tr'(t)/r(t) are both decreasing in t.
